blocks.title: Separation of variables
blocks.md: If $\frac{dy}{dx}=f(x)\,g(y)$ then $\int\frac{1}{g(y)}dy=\int f(x)\,dx$. Integrate both sides (one constant $C$ is enough), then use the initial condition to find $C$, then make $y$ the subject if possible.

blocks.title: Standard models
blocks.md: Growth/decay: $\frac{dP}{dt}=kP$ has solution $P=P_0e^{kt}$. Newton's law of cooling: $\frac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-T_s)$ with surroundings $T_s$, solution $T=T_s+(T_0-T_s)e^{-kt}$.

blocks.caption: Newton cooling: the temperature falls towards the room temperature of 25 degrees C.
blocks.alt: Decaying exponential curve from 95 degrees C levelling off at 25 degrees C, with the point (15.4, 40) marked.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Putting $C$ on both sides or forgetting it.
- Integrating the wrong side: all $y$ terms with $dy$, all $x$ terms with $dx$.
- In modelling, forgetting the units of $t$ or the sign of $k$.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A population of bacteria satisfies $\frac{dP}{dt}=0.05P$ with $P=1000$ at $t=0$. When does it double?

blocks.title: Sign change
blocks.md: If $f$ is continuous and $f(a)$, $f(b)$ have opposite signs then $f(x)=0$ has a root between $a$ and $b$. Repeating (interval bisection) narrows the root. Always say 'continuous'.

blocks.title: Iteration and Newton-Raphson
blocks.md: Rearrange $f(x)=0$ as $x=g(x)$ and iterate $x_{n+1}=g(x_n)$; it converges if $|g'|<1$ near the root. Newton-Raphson: $x_{n+1}=x_n-\frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$ (tangent meets the x-axis). It can fail if $f'(x_n)$ is near 0 or if the start is poor.

blocks.title: Trapezium rule
blocks.md: $\int_a^bf(x)\,dx\approx\frac h2\Big[y_0+y_n+2(y_1+\cdots+y_{n-1})\Big]$ with $n$ strips of width $h=\frac{b-a}{n}$. More strips give a better estimate.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md: In the trapezium rule the middle values are DOUBLED, the end values counted once. A calculator must be in radian mode for trig functions. Newton-Raphson needs $f'$: do not forget to differentiate correctly.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Use Newton-Raphson on $f(x)=x^3-x-2$ with $x_0=1.5$ to find $x_1$ and $x_2$.
